question.text: The collateral available for margin purposes in ETIRD must include at least what percentage in cash or cash equivalents?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per pages 257-259 of the NISM Series IV workbook, at least 50% of liquid assets at the clearing-member level must be in the form of the cash component / cash equivalents. Page 268 confirms the 50% cash-equivalent collateral rule applies at the clearing-member level and is not applied at the individual client level. Government of India securities are included in the cash component along with cash, fixed deposits, and bank guarantees. The Trap: 100% cash is not required. The 50% threshold is measured at the clearing-member/liquid-assets level, not the client level. The non-cash component, which can make up the balance, draws from the source-listed non-cash assets such as approved equity shares and corporate bonds subject to haircuts and limits. Note: Government securities sit inside the cash component per pages 257-259 of Series IV; the non-cash component covers the remaining balance using other approved liquid assets.
